newsitem.title: FRANCE: French special effects firm Duran Duboi to float.
newsitem.headline: French special effects firm Duran Duboi to float.

text.p: Shares in French special effects company Duran Duboi will be offered on the Paris bourse's Nouveau Marche next Tuesday at a price to be set between 152 francs ($26.64) and 225 francs a share, the company's founders said.

Duran Duboi, which works mainly for French television stations Canal Plus and La Cinquieme and film studios Gaumont and Fox, had turnover of 88.6 million francs in the year to September 30, 1996. It posted a loss of 1.14 million francs for the period.
Pascal Herold, one of the founders, told a news conference on Wednesday the company expects to have steady turnover growth.
It is aiming for turnover of 112 million francs in the current year, 138 million in the year 1997/98 and over 160 million francs in 1998/99, he said.
Last year's loss was due to major spending on advertising and television films, he said.
Duran Duboi's founders are seeking funds from the market because they prefer to limit the company's dependence on its banks, they said.
The company is currently working on special effects for Alien 8, a deal worth 12 million francs. DT/SLA ($ = 5.705 French Francs)
